sides.name: French Empire (Napoleon)
sides.note: Tech override per derived:tech-anchor (SOURCES.md anchor table, interpolated by year); air and cyber 0 = derived:absent-in-era. Ratings per derived:rating-rubric. 72,000-73,000: 48,950-50,600 infantry, 14,390-15,765 cavalry, 246-252 guns (Clodfelter, Bodart). Heavy/light cavalry split (cuirassiers, carabiniers, Guard heavy vs lancers, chasseurs, hussars) roughly half each, educated guess. Command 0.7: Napoleon slow to start (ground drying), Ney's unsupported cavalry charges, Grouchy's 33,000 detached. Training 0.7: veteran cadres but a hastily rebuilt army.

sides.name: Seventh Coalition (Wellington, Blucher)
sides.note: Tech override per derived:tech-anchor (SOURCES.md anchor table, interpolated by year); air and cyber 0 = derived:absent-in-era. Ratings per derived:rating-rubric. Initial force = Wellington's army ~68,000 (Clodfelter 67,661: 49,608 infantry, 12,408 cavalry, 5,645 artillerymen), 156 guns; heavy/light cavalry split educated guess. Prussians (~48,000 engaged of ~50,000): Bulow's IV Corps attacked Plancenoit at 16:30 (day 0.21 after a ~11:30 start), Zieten's I Corps and part of Pirch's II Corps engaged about 18:00-19:00 (day 0.29). Per-corps split of the Prussian total is an educated guess; 44 guns in action (Clodfelter) to 126 present (Bowden). Training 0.6: British/KGL core, inexperienced Dutch-Belgian, Hanoverian and Landwehr units. Hougoumont and La Haye Sainte were fortified farms (not a fortified city).

outcome.note: Coalition victory. French ~25,000 killed or wounded plus 8,000 captured (6,000-7,000 of them wounded), i.e. 26,000-27,000; Barbero 24,000-26,000; high counts captured separately. 15,000 deserted after the battle (not counted). Coalition 24,000: Wellington 17,000, Prussians 6,604-7,000. Start contested (10:00-13:00, ~11:30 usual), ended after 21:00. Rain the night before: muddy ground.
